title: Reconstruct Parentheses From Depths
description:
In a valid balanced parentheses string `s`, the nesting depth of each character is defined as follows: scanning left to right with open-count `open` initially `0`, an opening `'('` increments `open` by `1` and has depth `open`; a closing `')'` has depth `open` and then decrements `open` by `1`.

Given an integer array `depths`, reconstruct and return the unique valid balanced parentheses string `s` whose character depths equal `depths`, or return an empty string `""` if no valid balanced parentheses string has those depths.
hints: Track the current open count `open` starting at 0: at each position `i`, `'('` uniquely requires `depths[i] == open + 1` while `')'` uniquely requires `depths[i] == open` (with `open > 0`).
If `depths[i]` matches neither `open + 1` nor `open` (when `open > 0`), or if `open != 0` at the end, no valid string exists.

examples.explanation: Open transitions 0->1('('), 1->2('('), 2->1(')'), 1->0(')') yield depths [1, 2, 2, 1], uniquely giving "(())".
Open transitions 0->1, 1->0, 0->1, 1->0 yield depths [1, 1, 1, 1], uniquely giving "()()".
Jumping from depth 1 directly to depth 3 is impossible, so return "".
